pr_body:
# Objective

In #13343, `WorldQuery::get_state` was constrained from `&World` as the argument to `&Components`, but `WorldQuery::init_state` hasn't yet been changed from `&mut World` to match.

Fixes #13358

## Solution

Create a wrapper around `&mut Components` and `&mut Storages` that can be obtained from `&mut World` with a `component_initializer` method. 
This new `ComponentInitializer` re-exposes the API on `&mut Components` minus the `&mut Storages` parameter where it was present. For the `&Components` API, it simply derefs to its `components` field. 

## Changelog

### Added
The `World::component_initializer` method.
The `ComponentInitializer` struct that re-exposes `Components` API.
### Changed
`WorldQuery::init_state` now takes `&mut ComponentInitializer` instead of `&mut World`.

## Migration Guide
Instead of passing `&mut World` to `WorldQuery::init_state` directly, pass in a mutable reference to the struct returned from `World::component_initializer`.

issue_context.title: `WorldQuery::init_state` signature is too generous
issue_context.body:
> I realized that because `Storages` and `Components` aren't public fields on `World`, and there are no mutable accessor functions, doing the same change likely doesn't work for `init_state`. 
> Adding mutable accessor function does not make sense, because this would allow users to readily cause UB.
Instead we could have a function on `&mut World` that returns an opaque struct on which `init_component`, ... can be called.

_Originally posted by @Victoronz in https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/13343#issuecomment-2107782171_
comments: @Victoronz do you want to tackle this?

Sure, as I'm already familiar with this.

Currently I'd suggest a `component_initializer` method on `&mut World`. It would return a `ComponentInitializer` struct, which would be a wrapper around `&mut Components` and `&mut Storages`. This struct would re-expose all methods on `Components`, minus the `&mut Storages` parameter on `init_component` and `init_component_with_descriptor` respectively.
Sounds great: I look forward to reviewing it.
Maybe this should be punted off of 0.14, because the `bevy-trait-query` matter has made this more involved. A note could be put in the method comment in the meantime.
Agreed: we should bump this to 0.15.

According to https://github.com/JoJoJet/bevy-trait-query/issues/59#issuecomment-2212516814, the caching isn't actually required to make `bevy_trait_query` work. It's a wash performance-wise.

Maybe we should allow it anyways, but that's a major relief for me.

If it wasn't required, I think it is best to constrain the function again.
A superficial search on Github for `WorldQuery::init_state` impls has not turned up any further outliers for me, and the ones I knew for `get_state` seem to no longer be present either (presumably because of the update).

> Closing as fixed.

How so? I was under the impression that the solution to this is blocked on Resources-as-Entities, and will remain reverted until then.
It does definitely not belong to the current milestone though.
